story.title: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion to New Mexico for misleading consumers about data privacy - CBS News

facts.text: Meta was ordered to pay $25 billion in penalties by a New Mexico court on Wednesday as part of a data privacy case that stemmed from the company's Cambridge Analytica scandal from nearly a decade ago.
The Wednesday filing showed that the state was awarded $219.5 billion, but the penalty was ultimately reduced to $25 billion.

That scandal rocked the Mark Zuckerberg -led company before its official name change to Meta, and focused on allegations that the political consulting firm Cambridge Analytica improperly accessed the information of 87 million users , raising questions about Facebook's data handling practices.
Meta said it disagreed with that New Mexico ruling and planned to appeal.

"The extraordinary number of willful violations found by the jury, the duration and repetition of the conduct, the breadth of subjects on which violations occurred, the involvement of senior Facebook leadership, the size of New Mexico audiences reached, and the clear intentional and systematic nature of Facebook's repeated misstatements established in the trial record support the highest level of penalty allowed by the New Mexico Unfair Practices Act - $5,000 per violation found by the jury," New Mexico District Court Judge Francis Mathew wrote in the filing.
He added that "this penalty order demonstrates that those violations carry real consequences."
A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion after a jury found the company guilty of misleading consumers about the privacy of their data a decade ago.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Meta shares were climbing 1.77% and clocked in above $706.5 a piece at 3:01 p.m.
New Mexico was also at the helm of a landmark case against Meta and centered on social media addiction.
"Facebook's wrongdoing — over the course of years and systematically broadcast to the public — goes to the heart of Facebook's core business practices," Judge Francis Mathew said in the order.

Interest on the penalty would accrue during an appeal, but the number of violations Meta is charged with could be reduced.Meta attorney Matt Nicholson argued in court that a sum as high as $40 billion would be "shocking to the conscience" while an attorney for New Mexico, Randi McGinn, urged standing up to "tech titans who think they are bulletproof and can do whatever they want."Company argues that the state failed to prove harmThe state's case focused on accusations that Facebook deceived users about a data breach stemming from a third-party personality quiz that harvested data from roughly 87 million profiles and sold it to a political consulting firm, Cambridge Analytica, to generate targeted ads.
Eight years on, Cambridge Analytica is costing Meta more than any settlement: A court in the U.S. state of New Mexico has just ordered the Facebook parent to pay a penalty of $25 billion.
The New Mexico penalty is five times as large.
Torrez sees it as a warning to the entire tech industry, explicitly including social media and A.I. companies.
At the heart of the case is the Cambridge Analytica scandal.
New Mexico sued in 2021, accusing Facebook of misleading users for years about how it handled their data.
Statements about its handling of misinformation and hate speech were also part of the lawsuit.
Prosecutors said the company made 26 misleading statements about data privacy over 11 years.
New Mexico deliberately chose not to join the joint settlement and took its claims to trial instead.
According to New York Attorney General Letitia James , who led a coalition of 51 attorneys general in total, Meta will pay at least $12.1 billion and up to $17.1 billion.
